label: Transit Map
mood: the place of the event drawn as a diagram — a metro map in the modernist manner: thick lines in a few flat colours that run only horizontally, vertically and at 45°, with bends of one radius, page-coloured station dots, capsule interchanges and a numbered bullet at each line end, the lines running off the sheet wherever the page is free; one interchange is picked out in the accent and flagged with the venue from the poster's own copy, the date and time under it, and a few other stations take words of the headline. Also a single route that winds to the venue in numbered stops, and a street map of tinted blocks with a river, a park, one main road in the accent and a pin on the venue's block. Vector (SVG) in the poster's own text face, laid out on an invisible grid from hand-designed skeletons; where `numerals` makes the date the picture, this makes the place the picture. Good for anything people have to find their way to: exhibitions and openings, concerts and festivals, markets and pop-ups, conferences and meet-ups, open days and campus events, neighbourhood and city events, tours and travel.

lines.note: metro: how many lines, 3–5 (a skeleton draws as many as it holds: the ring three, the others four; the triangle takes a fifth along the foot)

map.note: metro: the skeleton — triangle | junction | ring; empty = picked by the seed (a strip of a room always gets the flat three-line map)

stops.note: route: how many numbered stops, the venue included (5–7); empty = picked by the seed

names.note: how many other stations / stops / blocks take a short word from the copy (0–5)

metro.note: three to five lines crossing at a few interchanges, some running side by side; one interchange is the venue — a larger marker in the accent with a flag carrying the venue's name, the date and time under it. A few stations are named with words of the headline, line ends carry numbered bullets, and lines run off the page edge where the layout leaves it free

route.note: a single thick line that winds across the box in long straight runs and 45° bends (a step, a hairpin or an S, by the shape of the room) with five to seven numbered stops, the last one the venue, marked in the accent and flagged; the words of the headline name stops on the way

blocks.note: a street map from above that fills the free part of the page and runs off its edge: city blocks as flat tints with paper-coloured streets on a slightly irregular grid, one 45° avenue, a river as one calm band with bridges, a park, one main road in the accent, and a map pin on the venue's block with its flag; a few blocks carry a word of the headline like a district name
